purpose: Prevent historical US/British submarine sinkings from being inherited one-for-one where Branch Tokai/Ka-go/escort/COMSEC coverage exists.
Carry Japanese ASW effects into US submarine physical and effective-patrol wallets.
Require an explicit local ASW sortie/coverage check whenever future Allied submarine activity is adjudicated.

merchant_loss_reaudit.principle: Do not add a second blanket merchant-fleet bonus. Current Branch early-1944 merchant/tanker afloat bands are already substantially healthier than historical. Reallocate part of that preservation to ASW and re-adjudicate individual submarine attacks instead.
merchant_loss_reaudit.historical_anchor: US submarines sank about 1.342 million tons of Japanese merchant shipping >=1000 tons in 1943 in the US Navy official report.
guards: These percentages apply to US-submarine-caused merchant losses or attack realization, not to all Japanese shipping losses from all causes.
Do not apply both the global and priority-lane reductions to the same event.
Higher Japanese target density from preserved shipping partly offsets the ASW improvement; do not convert attack-opportunity reduction directly into the same percentage of GRT saved.
COMSEC benefit enters as fewer well-cued ambushes, not as a sensor bonus.

US_submarine_wallet_working.historical_equivalent_estimate_note: Exact date-specific Pacific US submarine hull roster remains to be rebuilt; use a band until a hull-by-hull ledger is made.
US_submarine_wallet_working.interpretation: The Branch does not cripple US submarine force generation. It trims local simultaneous coverage and patrol-days enough to matter at operational gates.

future_event_gate: Was a Tokai detachment physically based within useful radius on the date?
How many serviceable aircraft and trained crews were available?
Was the mission convoy-front sweep, harbor/strait barrier, datum localization, or open-ocean search?
Was there a radar/visual/DF datum to hand to MAD?
Did surface escorts/shore plot receive the contact in time?

clock.1943: practical Akitsu Maru air unit centered; land artillery-observation use also exists

Ka_go.maritime_role: Short-range convoy-near contact holding, marking and handoff; not a Tokai substitute and not a helicopter.
Ka_go.typical_Akitsu_Maru_load: 4-6 Ka-go if retaining amphibious function; 6-8 in convoy-escort emphasis; 8-10 only with strong ASW-carrier specialization cost.
Ka_go.MAD_state: 1944 lightweight MAD is trial-level; normal maritime ASW uses visual/radio/marker and cueing from mother ship/other aircraft.
future_event_gate: Was Akitsu Maru or another physically valid Ka-go unit actually assigned to this convoy/area?
Was continuous daylight coverage generated or only short sorties?
Did Ka-go hold/mark a datum long enough for fixed-wing aircraft or escorts to attack?

mandatory_checks_before_adjudication: historical contact cause: routine patrol, COMINT cue, reconnaissance cue, or special operation
Branch high-grade COMINT inheritance allowed or forbidden
Ka-go/Akitsu Maru local presence if relevant
escort sonar/depth-charge readiness and escort count
shore radar/DF/plot or convoy reporting network
attack denial, reattack denial, damage, mission kill, kill as separate outputs
generic_Allied_submarine_event_rule.default: No Allied submarine sinking is inherited solely because it occurred historically.

HAILSTONE_escape_route_correction.previous_center: one 4,000-7,000 GRT merchant/auxiliary sunk by US submarine during final Truk evacuation
HAILSTONE_escape_route_correction.revised_center: 0 sunk centered; one credible attack opportunity remains, with 1 ship sunk/CTL as a substantial upper branch
HAILSTONE_escape_route_correction.reason: Truk is a priority base and 1944-Feb Tokai local sortie/sweep is plausible; exit-barrier US submarines remain dangerous but are less likely to hold an undisturbed firing position.
